subject: Telemetry runbook ownership & escalation agreement
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@grafana.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry runbook ownership & escalation agreement

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the initial sync last week. Attached is a first-pass runbook and a simple SLA/escalation matrix we drafted for customers using the Grafana + Redwood telemetry bridge (OpenTelemetry -> Datadog/Grafana paths).

High-level asks: 
- Can Redwood confirm which ownership lane you want for instrumentation SDK issues vs connector config?
- Proposed escalation tiers are in the matrix (Redwood L1, Partner L2, Grafana L3). Would like your feedback on routing and on-call handoffs.
- We think adding a "security review" checkpoint for private deployments is necessary — any objections?

Proposed times for a 30-min alignment this week: Thu 08:00-10:00 PT, Fri 11:00-13:00 PT.

Attachments: redwood-grafana-runbook-draft.md, sla-escalation-matrix.xlsx

Cheers,
Elaine Park
Partner Solutions Engineer, Grafana Labs
elaine.park@grafana.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@grafana.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry runbook ownership & escalation agreement

Thanks Elaine — good draft, appreciate the structure. Quick responses inline and proposed edits below.

- Ownership lanes: Redwood will own "instrumentation SDK compatibility/support" (we handle SDK releases, major regressions, and customer upgrade guidance). Redwood asks Grafana to own connector deployment/configuration and dashboards in Grafana Cloud for joint customers.
- Escalation routing: the matrix looks reasonable but we propose the following tweak: Redwood on-call should triage and create an internal incident ticket that references the Grafana incident ID before escalation to Grafana L3 (helps with auditing).
- Security review: agree — we want a short checklist that includes data retention settings, prefix/KV cache behaviors, and KMS key handling for Private deployments. Redwood can own the checklist but will need a Grafana sign-off.

I'm looping in Marissa (alliances) and Ben (solutions) to validate SLAs and field handoffs.

My availability for a quick 30-min sync: Thu 09:30-10:30 PT, Fri 11:30-12:30 PT. If those don't work, propose times and we'll adapt.

Next steps I will take after we agree: 1) update the runbook with the triage workflow; 2) add the security checklist; 3) circulate a single-line acceptance for both parties to sign off.

— Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry runbook ownership & escalation agreement

Quick note — +1 on the security checklist. Also suggest we include an explicit "upgrade window" clause for connector patches that require coordinated downtime (even if brief). That will help field teams set customer expectations. Happy to draft the clause after the call.

- Marissa
Director, Alliances
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@grafana.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datadog.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry runbook ownership & escalation agreement

Logan — thanks, that plan works for us. I've looped in Samir from Datadog because several large prospects route OTLP to Datadog before Grafana for dashboards; this will help align cross-product escalation and avoid ping-pong during incidents.

Samir: quick intro — we are aligning an ownership and escalation runbook between Redwood and Grafana for the telemetry bridge. Could you confirm Datadog's expectation for incident IDs and whether Datadog requires a separate routed ticket before Grafana engagement?

We can do Fri 11:30 PT — I'll take it.

Elaine
Partner Solutions Engineer, Grafana Labs
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@grafana.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@datadog.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 23:43:00 +00:00
Subject: Finalized: Telemetry runbook ownership & escalation agreement (action required)

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Attached is the updated runbook and the SLA/escalation matrix reflecting the triage step, upgrade window clause, and the security checklist placeholder. Please review and reply with a single-line "approve" so we can lock it in and publish to the partner-runbook Drive folder.

Attachments: redwood-grafana-runbook-draft.md, sla-escalation-matrix.xlsx
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-grafana-runbooks
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/98765

Planned next steps after approvals:
- Logan: publish final runbook to public partner docs and notify field enablement (2 business days)
- Marissa: draft the upgrade window clause language and add to the runbook (1 business day)
- Elaine: confirm Grafana on-call rotation and provide L3 contact details (1 business day)
- Samir: confirm Datadog ticketing expectations for routed incidents (2 business days)

If no objections by EOD Tue 2027-08-03 we will consider this accepted and move to publication.

— Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
